verified.notes: Fetched Electrek 2025-09-03. Excerpt verbatim on page: 'The Longquan II is a 10-Ah all-solid-state cell with an energy density of up to 300 Wh/kg.' and 'mass production of these ultra-dense cells will eventually power humanoid robots, uncrewed aerial vehicles, and AI equipment.' Numbers 10 Ah and 300 Wh/kg verbatim. Forward-looking 'will eventually power' — limitations field already flags it as intended/future, not current shipment. Capability/intent evidence, not an OEM PO. Correctly modeled.

Fetched Molicel /about/. 'ultra-high power cylindrical cells' verbatim; humanoid relevance verbatim and even more specific than excerpt: 2025 timeline 'INR-21700-P50B has been adopted for humanoid robotics applications'; 'MOLICEL is part of Taiwan Cement Corporation (TCC) Group' verbatim. Vendor self-description (vendor_claim) — application category, not an OEM design-win, as limitations state. No quantitative claim in the excerpt, so numberInQuote=false.

Fetched Panasonic newsroom en251125-2. Excerpt verbatim: 'Panasonic Energy's 2170 cells, offering superior energy density, safety and reliability, are crucial for Zoox's high-performance robotaxis.' CONFIRMED: zero humanoid mention; application is unambiguously Zoox ROBOTAXI (wheeled vehicle), not a humanoid robot. Record correctly models this as 2170 cylindrical form-factor capability evidence only — edge claim explicitly states 'a confirmed Panasonic supply to a named humanoid OEM was not found' and context labels it 'capability evidence, not a humanoid purchase order.' No humanoid over-claim. '2170' is a format designator, not a quantitative metric at a basis, so numberInQuote=false.

Fetched Yahoo Finance mirror of Infineon Business Wire release; full body text resolves (not a stub). Excerpt verbatim: 'Infineon enables the key functional blocks in humanoid robots with a broad portfolio of dedicated products and technologies - from power switches to microcontrollers, sensors and connectivity.' NVIDIA Jetson Thor partnership confirmed in body. NUANCE for owner: the release frames 'dedicated' as existing product families (PSOC, AURIX, CoolGaN, XENSIV) applied to / 'dedicated solutions for' humanoid robots, NOT silicon exclusively designed only for humanoids. The stored excerpt is verbatim-accurate and the edge context already says the BMS firmware is the integrator's (captive). Edge claim phrase 'humanoid-dedicated product line' is supported by the press release's own 'dedicated products and technologies ... humanoid robots' language but should be read as dedicated-portfolio-positioning, not humanoid-exclusive parts. No quantitative figure in excerpt, numberInQuote=false.

Fetched NXP gitbook rddrone-bms772. Excerpt verbatim: 'The RDDRONE-BMS772 is a standalone BMS Reference Design suitable for mobile robotics such as drones and rovers, supporting 3-6 cell batteries.' Cell-count '3-6 cells' confirmed verbatim at the stated basis; application 'mobile robotics such as drones and rovers' verbatim. Humanoid relevance is by category adjacency only (mobile robotics, not humanoid specifically) — limitations field correctly states this; reference design / merchant silicon, not a confirmed humanoid pack supply. numberInQuote=true for the 3-6 cell figure.
